newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says Lake victim of political destruction.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says Lake victim of political destruction.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Tuesday that Tony Lake's withdrawal from consideration to be CIA director was a real loss to the country, and blamed a cycle of "political destruction" for Lake's decision.

"For too long, we have allowed ordinary political processes and honest disagreements among honourable people to descend into political sniping, then into political revenge, and too often that results in political destruction," Clinton said in a statement to reporters in the White House residence.

Clinton said he had been prepared to fight for Lake, his former national security adviser, for as long as it took to win him Senate confirmation, but Lake was concerned about the effect of a protracted confirmation fight on the CIA.

"I think he was afraid the longer this went on ... the more it would damage the agency," said the president, who is recovering from knee surgery and sat in a chair with his right foot on a stool. He summoned reporters to hear his personal statement on a nomination withdrawal that stunned Washington.

Lake informed Clinton on Monday evening that he was withdrawing from the Senate confirmation process because he felt he had become a political football for Republicans in Congress. Clinton, a Democrat, described Lake on Tuesday as "a professional, a patriot and a statesman."
"I respect his decision because nobody should have to endure what he has endured in the course of this nomination, but make no mistake about it, it's a loss for the country," the president said.
